trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Vatican City, Borgo district Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to hotel in Vatican City, Borgo district. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino to Termini (~14€), then Metro Line A to Ottaviano station (~1.50€). Check in and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel, then take a relaxed orientation stroll through the Borgo district. Walk along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square for your first iconic view of St. Peter's Basilica. Entry to the Basilica itself is FREE — explore the stunning interior at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the charming streets of Prati neighborhood, just north of the Borgo. Browse local shops and soak in the atmosphere. Enjoy a sunset view of Castel Sant'Angelo from Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge — completely free and spectacular.

meals.breakfast: N/A (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable bite near the airport or at Termini station — try a panino or pizza al taglio for around 3–5€.
meals.dinner: Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria, Prati) — Rome's legendary pizza al taglio spot. Pay by weight, budget around 8–12€ for a satisfying meal. Arrive early as it gets busy.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to travel fatigue. Purchase a 48-hour or 72-hour public transport pass (6€ / 11€) at Termini for convenience. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance. June in Rome is warm (25–32°C), so carry water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel — book tickets online in advance to skip the long queues (20€ standard entry). Arrive right at opening (9:00 AM) for smaller crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the incredible art collections, Egyptian antiquities, and Raphael Rooms before reaching the breathtaking Sistine Chapel.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the museums, visit St. Peter's Basilica again (FREE) and this time climb to the top of St. Peter's Dome for panoramic views of Rome (8€ on foot, 10€ by elevator). Have a picnic lunch in the nearby Parco Adriano green area to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Cross the Tiber and explore the lively Trastevere neighborhood on foot. Stroll through its cobblestone alleys, visit the beautiful Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica (FREE), and enjoy the vibrant evening street atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bar or café near the hotel — cornetto (croissant) + cappuccino for 1.50–2.50€. Avoid tourist-facing cafés on Via della Conciliazione.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local alimentari (deli) — bread, cheese, cured meats, and fruit for under 7€. Eat in Parco Adriano.
meals.dinner: Trattoria Da Enzo al 29 (Trastevere) — authentic Roman cuisine at fair prices. Expect cacio e pepe or coda alla vaccinara for 10–14€ per dish. Budget around 18–22€ total with house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except last Sunday of the month, which is FREE but extremely crowded). Book tickets at least a few days ahead online to avoid same-day surcharges. Dress code required: covered shoulders and knees for the Basilica.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the historic center via Metro or a scenic 30-minute walk. Visit the Pantheon (5€ entry — great value for one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings). Arrive early (opens 9:00 AM) before tour groups flood in. Spend time admiring the oculus and Roman engineering marvel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Piazza Navona (FREE) — one of Rome's most beautiful baroque squares, featuring Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. Then explore the nearby Campo de' Fiori market square. Continue to the stunning Palazzo Farnese exterior (free to admire from outside) and the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood for a fascinating historical walk.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the Trevi Fountain (FREE) as the sun sets — the golden light makes it magical. Toss a coin! Then walk to the Spanish Steps (FREE) for a classic Roman evening. Browse the lively streets around Via del Corso.

meals.breakfast: Café Sant'Eustachio (Piazza Sant'Eustachio) — famous for arguably Rome's best coffee. Gran caffè costs ~2€ standing at the bar. A Roman institution.
meals.lunch: Pizza al taglio from a local bakery near Campo de' Fiori — 5–8€ for a filling slice selection.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Ingegno or a simple trattoria near the Pantheon. Alternatively, grab a budget-friendly meal at a local rosticceria (roast chicken shop) for 8–10€.

day_by_day.notes: The historic center is best explored on foot — everything is within 15–20 minutes of each other. Avoid overpriced restaurants immediately adjacent to major monuments. Look for restaurants on side streets with menus in Italian (not just English) for better value.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Colosseo station and visit the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill — all covered by one combined ticket (18€, book online to skip queues). Spend the morning exploring ancient Rome's most iconic ruins. Arrive at 9:00 AM opening time.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Forum, walk up Capitoline Hill (Campidoglio) for a free panoramic view over the Roman Forum. Visit the exterior of the Circus Maximus (FREE) — the ancient chariot racing stadium. Walk through the atmospheric Aventine Hill neighborhood and visit the Knights of Malta Keyhole (FREE) for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere or explore Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic food quarter. Visit the Testaccio Market (closes by afternoon, good for a late browse) and enjoy the local vibe away from tourist crowds.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a nearby bar for 2–3€.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the Colosseum visit — no affordable food inside. Buy supplies at a nearby alimentari beforehand.
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — beloved local trattoria known for classic Roman offal dishes and pasta. Budget 18–25€ per person. Alternatively, Roscioli Salumeria for gourmet sandwiches around 8–10€.

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum complex requires significant walking on uneven surfaces — wear comfortable shoes. Combined tickets include the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill, so maximize your visit. Book Colosseum tickets at least 2–3 days in advance, especially in June.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art museums housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings (21€, MUST book in advance as entry is strictly timed in 2-hour slots). Located in the beautiful Villa Borghese park. Arrive for the 9:00 AM slot.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a free afternoon stroll through the vast Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's answer to Central Park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (about 3€ per person) or simply relax. Walk down the scenic Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Piazza del Popolo and Rome's rooftops.
day_by_day.evening: Descend into Piazza del Popolo (FREE) — a grand Renaissance square with twin baroque churches. Explore the surrounding streets of Flaminio neighborhood. Head back toward the center via Via del Corso for evening shopping and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Picnic supplies from a local supermarket (Conad or Carrefour) — yogurt, fruit, pastries for under 4€. Enjoy in Villa Borghese.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — buy fresh supplies from the Prati neighborhood market or a nearby deli. Budget 6–8€.
meals.dinner: Osteria Barberini or explore the Pigneto neighborhood (a 20-minute bus ride) for authentic, affordable Roman dining popular with locals. Budget 15–20€.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance in summer — book as soon as possible. The gallery only admits 360 visitors at a time. Villa Borghese is perfect for a midday rest in the shade during Rome's June heat.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Trastevere neighborhood properly in the morning when it's quieter. Visit the stunning interior of Santa Cecilia in Trastevere church (small donation suggested) and the Botanical Garden of Rome (Orto Botanico, 8€) — a peaceful green escape with over 3,000 plant species.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross back over the Tiber and visit the lesser-known but magnificent Palazzo Doria Pamphilj art gallery (12€) — home to an extraordinary private collection including Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X, with far fewer crowds than major museums. Then browse the antique market at Porta Portese if it's a Sunday (Saturdays have a smaller market at Via Sannio).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy your last full evening with a sunset aperitivo — a Roman tradition. Head to a bar in Prati or Trastevere for a spritz (3–5€) which often comes with free snacks. Take a final evening walk along the Tiber riverbanks, beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Bar Marzapane or a local Trastevere café — cornetto and cappuccino for 2€.
meals.lunch: Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello in Trastevere for a sit-down Roman lunch. Many offer a fixed-price lunch menu (pranzo fisso) for 10–12€ including primo, secondo, and water.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your second-to-last night — try Supplì Roma (Trastevere branch) for Rome's best supplì (fried rice balls, 2€ each) and street food, keeping the total under 15€, or a neighborhood trattoria for 20–25€.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday evenings in Trastevere are very lively but also very crowded. Restaurants fill up fast — consider booking dinner in advance or eating slightly earlier (7:00–7:30 PM) before the main rush. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take advantage of the FREE last Sunday of the month entry to state museums (if applicable — check the calendar). If not, revisit your favorite free sites: St. Peter's Square for a quiet morning reflection, or the Castel Sant'Angelo exterior and bridge. Visit the Sunday morning market at Porta Portese flea market in Trastevere (7:00 AM–2:00 PM) — Rome's largest and most famous flea market, great for souvenirs and browsing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon exploration: revisit any missed sights or simply wander through your favorite neighborhoods. Consider a gelato tour — compare authentic gelaterias (look for natural colors and gelato stored in covered metal containers). Try Fatamorgana (artisan flavors) or Gelateria dei Gracchi (near the hotel) — 2.50–3.50€ per cone.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Prati neighborhood close to the hotel for convenience. Pack bags and prepare for departure. Take a final evening walk to the illuminated Castel Sant'Angelo for a memorable last image of Rome.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed breakfast at a local bar near the hotel — enjoy your last Roman cornetto and espresso for 2€.
meals.lunch: Porta Portese market area street food, or a quick trattoria lunch in Trastevere for 10–12€.
meals.dinner: Il Sorpasso (Prati) — a beloved local wine bar and restaurant with excellent cicchetti (small bites) and affordable full meals. Budget 18–22€. Perfect for a relaxed farewell dinner near the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Check flight departure time and plan airport transfer accordingly. Leonardo Express trains run every 30 minutes from Termini to Fiumicino (~14€). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for travel and check-in. Keep some coins for luggage lockers or tips. The last Sunday of the month offers free entry to many national museums — a great budget bonus if your trip aligns.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (~30 min), then a taxi or bus to your Borgo district boutique hotel near the Vatican. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Neighborhood Orientation Walk: After settling in, take a leisurely stroll through the Borgo district and along the Tiber River. Visit Castel Sant'Angelo (exterior and optional quick entry, ~€15) for stunning views of Rome. Walk across Ponte Sant'Angelo to admire the angel sculptures. This gentle introduction keeps you close to the hotel after a long travel day.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk: Join the guided evening walk through Trastevere's cobblestone streets, sampling supplì, Roman artichokes, local cheeses, and regional wines. A perfect low-effort, high-reward first evening that lets you taste authentic Roman street food without needing to plan a full dinner separately.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick espresso and cornetto at a bar near Roma Termini upon arrival (~€3–4)
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel after check-in — try a local bar or rosticceria in Borgo for a panino or slice of pizza al taglio (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Covered by the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk; supplement with a gelato from Fatamorgana or Fior di Luna in Trastevere (~€3)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 relaxed — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pre-book the Trastevere evening walk in advance as spots fill quickly in June. Wear comfortable walking shoes from the start. The Borgo district is extremely walkable to the Vatican and Castel Sant'Angelo.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Begin at 9:00 AM with a pre-booked skip-the-line ticket (~€27–35 or ~€50–70 for a guided tour). Spend 3–4 hours exploring the vast collections — the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Square: Exit the Museums directly into St. Peter's Basilica (free entry). Marvel at Michelangelo's Pietà, Bernini's baldachin, and climb the dome (~€8 with elevator, ~€6 on foot) for panoramic views over Rome. Spend 2 hours exploring at your own pace before the afternoon crowds thin out.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Prati neighborhood: Head to the upscale but accessible Prati district, just north of the Vatican, for a sit-down dinner. This area is beloved by locals and offers excellent mid-range trattorias away from tourist traps.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a classic Roman bar in Borgo — espresso, cornetto, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch inside the Vatican Museums café or grab a slice at a nearby Prati pizzeria al taglio like Pizzarium Bonci (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Settimio all'Arancio or a similar Prati trattoria — try cacio e pepe, carbonara, or saltimbocca alla romana with house wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most iconic and busiest day — book Vatican tickets at least 2–3 weeks ahead for June. Start as early as possible (opening is 9:00 AM). Dress code required for St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees. The Vatican Museums alone can take 3–5 hours; don't rush the Sistine Chapel.

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class: Head to the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market by 9:00 AM to select fresh seasonal produce, local cheeses, cured meats, and herbs with your cooking class instructor. Then move to a nearby kitchen studio for a 3-hour hands-on class learning to make fresh pasta, a Roman sauce, and a traditional dessert (~€80–120 per person). A highlight for food lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jewish Ghetto & Largo di Torre Argentina: After the cooking class, walk through Rome's ancient Jewish Ghetto neighborhood, one of the oldest in the world. Visit the open-air ruins of Largo di Torre Argentina (free) — the very site where Julius Caesar was assassinated — and meet the resident cat colony. Browse the Ghetto's Jewish bakeries for a sweet treat.
day_by_day.evening: Piazza Navona & Pantheon by Night: Stroll to the stunning Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers illuminated at night, then walk five minutes to the Pantheon (exterior at night is magical, free). Enjoy the lively atmosphere of this central neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market — espresso and pastry at a Borgo bar (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you prepared in the cooking class — this is typically included in the experience!
meals.dinner: Dinner near Piazza Navona — try Osteria dell'Anima or a similar mid-range osteria for Roman Jewish specialties like carciofi alla giudia (fried artichokes) and baccalà (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market runs Monday–Saturday mornings until about 2:00 PM. Book the cooking class well in advance. The Jewish Ghetto is a short 15-minute walk from Campo de' Fiori. Evenings around Piazza Navona can be lively and slightly touristy — arrive after 8:30 PM for a more atmospheric experience.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour: Take a taxi or bus to Villa Borghese for a 9:00 AM timed-entry slot at the Borghese Gallery (~€15 entry + ~€2 booking fee, or ~€40–60 for a guided tour). Admire Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases. Entry is strictly limited to 2 hours, making it an intimate and unhurried experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Pincian Hill: After the gallery, spend the afternoon exploring the vast Villa Borghese park on foot or by rented rowboat on the lake (~€5/30 min). Walk up to the Pincian Hill terrace for one of Rome's best panoramic views over Piazza del Popolo and the city skyline. Relax in the shade — a perfect mid-trip recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo & Dinner in Pigneto or Testaccio: Venture to the authentic Testaccio neighborhood, Rome's traditional working-class food district, for a classic Roman aperitivo hour followed by dinner at a local trattoria known for offal dishes, pasta, and wood-fired meats.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a café in Prati before heading to Villa Borghese (~€6–10)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in Villa Borghese park — pick up supplies from a nearby deli or Prati market: bread, cheese, prosciutto, fruit (~€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Testaccio trattoria such as Da Remo (pizza) or Flavio al Velavevodetto for Roman classics like rigatoni alla pajata or coda alla vaccinara (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery MUST be booked in advance — it sells out weeks ahead in June. Timed entry is strictly enforced; arrive 15 minutes early. The gallery only allows 360 visitors at a time, so it feels wonderfully uncrowded. Testaccio is about 30 minutes by bus or 15 minutes by taxi from the gallery.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk: Take the guided archaeological walk starting at 9:00 AM. Enter via the Colosseum combined ticket (~€16–22) and explore the Roman Forum's ancient temples, arches, and sacred roads, then climb Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Forum and Circus Maximus. Allow 3–3.5 hours for this immersive journey through ancient Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Colosseum Visit: Use your combined ticket to enter the iconic Colosseum (~€16–22, or upgrade to an underground/arena floor tour for ~€45). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the amphitheater's levels and learning about gladiatorial combat. Afterward, walk to the nearby Circus Maximus for a quiet moment at this ancient chariot-racing venue.
day_by_day.evening: Aventine Hill Sunset & Dinner in Trastevere: Walk up Aventine Hill to the famous Knights of Malta keyhole — peek through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Then descend into Trastevere for a relaxed dinner in one of Rome's most charming and atmospheric neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a quick bar stop near the Colosseum area (~€5–8)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick lunch near the Forum — try a nearby alimentari or trattoria in the Celio neighborhood for a simple pasta or sandwich (~€12–18)
meals.dinner: Trastevere restaurant such as Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello for authentic Roman pasta, grilled meats, and local Frascati wine (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum tickets online in advance — June is peak season and queues are enormous. The combined Forum/Palatine/Colosseum ticket is valid for 2 consecutive days. Wear sturdy shoes — the Forum and Palatine Hill involve uneven cobblestones and significant walking. The Aventine keyhole is free and worth the 10-minute detour.

day_by_day.morning: Trastevere Sunday Market & Piazza Santa Maria: Sunday morning is magical in Trastevere. Browse the Porta Portese flea market (Rome's largest, open Sunday mornings until 2:00 PM) for vintage finds, antiques, and local crafts. Then visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free) with its 12th-century golden mosaics — one of Rome's oldest and most beautiful churches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gianicolo Hill & Janiculum Terrace: Climb or take a short taxi ride to Gianicolo Hill for arguably the best panoramic view of Rome's rooftops and domes. Watch the traditional noon cannon firing (12:00 PM daily). Spend the afternoon wandering back downhill through the quieter streets of Trastevere and the Borgo district, visiting local artisan shops and galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Gelato Passeggiata: Enjoy a special farewell dinner at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant — perhaps near Piazza del Popolo or back in Prati. End the evening with a classic Roman passeggiata (evening stroll) along the Tiber River and a final gelato.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Trastevere before the market — try Bar San Calisto for a classic cheap Roman espresso experience (~€2–5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a Trastevere trattoria or enoteca — try supplì, bruschetta, and a glass of local white wine (~€15–22)
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Ristorante Il Sorpasso in Prati or similar — antipasti, handmade pasta, main course, dessert, and wine (~€40–55 per person for a special occasion)

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese is best visited early (8:00–10:00 AM) before it gets too crowded and hot. Sunday in Rome means many churches hold morning masses — respectful visitors are welcome. The Gianicolo noon cannon is a beloved Roman tradition since 1847. This is a wonderful slower day to soak in the city's rhythm before the final day.

day_by_day.morning: Piazza del Popolo & Santa Maria del Popolo Church: Start the final morning at the grand Piazza del Popolo, one of Rome's most elegant squares. Visit the Basilica di Santa Maria del Popolo (free) to see two extraordinary Caravaggio paintings — The Conversion of Saint Paul and The Crucifixion of Saint Peter — and Raphael's Chigi Chapel. A hidden gem beloved by art lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Stroll: Spanish Steps & Trevi Fountain: Walk to the Spanish Steps for a final view over the city, then continue to the Trevi Fountain to toss your coin and make your wish to return to Rome. Browse the nearby Via Condotti for window shopping or pick up last-minute gifts. Head back to the hotel to collect luggage.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final espresso and cornetto at a Borgo bar, then transfer to the airport. Take the Leonardo Express from Roma Termini or a pre-booked private transfer for a stress-free departure.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at a classic bar near the hotel — espresso doppio and a warm cornetto alla crema (~€4–6)
meals.lunch: Lunch near Trevi Fountain area — avoid tourist traps; instead try a side-street trattoria or a quality tavola calda for a final plate of pasta (~€15–22)
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or an early light dinner near Termini if time allows before departure (~€15–25)

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. The Trevi Fountain is extremely crowded in June — visit before 10:00 AM if possible or accept the crowds as part of the experience. Book airport transfer in advance for peace of mind. The Leonardo Express runs every 30 minutes from Termini to Fiumicino (~€14).

Admire the Castel Sant'Angelo from the outside, stroll along the scenic Lungotevere riverbank, and soak in your first impressions of Rome without any pressure. Stop at a local enoteca for a welcome Aperol Spritz or Negroni.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join an exclusive private evening food tour through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, local cheeses, and paired wines as the city glows in golden hour light. A perfect, low-key introduction to Roman culinary culture after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy breakfast on the plane or grab a quick espresso and cornetto at a Borgo café upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at Il Sorpasso (Prati district, 10-minute walk) — a beloved Roman bistro known for its charcuterie boards, seasonal vegetables, and natural wines. Perfect post-arrival fuel.
meals.dinner: Dinner included within the Trastevere Food & Wine Walk experience, or cap the evening at Ristorante Glass Hostaria (Michelin-starred, Trastevere) for a refined tasting menu showcasing modern Roman cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before 13:00 arrival. Keep Day 1 light and flexible to recover from travel. Confirm private transfer booking in advance. Trastevere is approximately 20 minutes by taxi or private car from the Borgo district.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (Private Early Access Tour) — Begin with an exclusive pre-opening or early-access private guided tour of the Vatican Museums, one of the world's greatest art collections. Walk through the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and culminate in a serene, crowd-free experience inside the Sistine Chapel marveling at Michelangelo's breathtaking ceiling frescoes. Being steps from your hotel makes this seamlessly convenient.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb — After the museums, walk directly to St. Peter's Basilica for a self-paced exploration of its awe-inspiring interior, including Michelangelo's Pietà. Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views over Rome. Afterward, enjoy a leisurely coffee break at a café in the Borgo Pio pedestrian lane.
day_by_day.evening: Fine Dining in Prati — Spend a relaxed evening in the upscale Prati neighborhood, just minutes from your hotel. Browse luxury boutiques along Via Cola di Rienzo before a sophisticated dinner reservation.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or at Sciascia Caffè (Prati) — one of Rome's most celebrated historic cafés, famous for its rich, chocolatey espresso and elegant atmosphere.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Il Matriciano (Prati) — a classic Roman trattoria beloved since 1957, known for cacio e pepe, carbonara, and amatriciana. A true institution steps from the Vatican.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Settimio all'Arancio or Ristorante Settimio (Prati/Centro) — elegant Roman cuisine in a refined setting. Alternatively, book a table at Osteria dell'Angelo for authentic Roman home cooking elevated to a premium experience.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Vatican Museums early-access or skip-the-line private tour well in advance — this is one of the most visited sites in the world. Your hotel's concierge can arrange this. Dress code applies for St. Peter's Basilica (covered shoulders and knees required).

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class — Begin your morning at the vibrant, colorful Campo de' Fiori market, selecting the finest seasonal produce, fresh pasta, local cheeses, and aromatic herbs alongside your private chef guide. Then transfer to a premium cooking studio for a hands-on Roman cooking class — crafting dishes like cacio e pepe, supplì, and a classic Roman dessert using the ingredients you personally selected.
day_by_day.afternoon: Jewish Ghetto & Renaissance Palaces Walking Tour — After your cooking class lunch, explore the historic Jewish Ghetto neighborhood and nearby Largo di Torre Argentina (ancient Roman temples and Julius Caesar's assassination site). Stroll past the elegant Palazzo Farnese and through the charming Piazza Navona, stopping to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers.
day_by_day.evening: Piazza Navona & Centro Storico Evening — As the sun sets over the baroque piazzas, enjoy aperitivo at a terrace bar overlooking Piazza Navona. Then wander through the atmospheric centro storico (historic center) at night, when Rome's ancient streets are beautifully illuminated.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or at Antico Forno Roscioli (Campo de' Fiori area) — Rome's legendary bakery serving extraordinary pastries, fresh bread, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch is the culminating feast of your cooking class — you eat what you cook, paired with selected Italian wines.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Piperno (Jewish Ghetto) — one of Rome's most historic and prestigious restaurants, renowned for its Roman-Jewish cuisine including the iconic carciofi alla giudia (deep-fried artichokes) and oxtail. Reserve well in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market is most lively between 8:00–13:00, so aim for an 8:30 start. Cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours. The Jewish Ghetto is approximately 20 minutes by taxi from your Borgo hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Private Art Tour — Secure an exclusive private guided tour of the magnificent Villa Borghese gallery, home to Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's most dramatic masterpieces. The gallery strictly limits visitor numbers, making this an intimate, world-class art experience. Arrive at opening for maximum tranquility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Pincio Terrace — After the gallery, spend a leisurely afternoon strolling through the beautifully manicured Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the ornamental lake, or simply relax in the shade of umbrella pines. Walk up to the Pincio Terrace for one of Rome's most spectacular panoramic views over Piazza del Popolo and the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury Spa & Rooftop Aperitivo — Return to your hotel area for a rejuvenating spa treatment (book at a nearby luxury hotel spa such as the Rome Cavalieri or a Prati wellness center). Then enjoy a sunset aperitivo from a rooftop bar with views of St. Peter's dome — a quintessential Roman luxury moment.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel — request a full Italian breakfast spread with fresh pastries, seasonal fruit, cold cuts, and quality espresso.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in the Villa Borghese gardens — arrange a premium picnic basket through your hotel concierge, filled with artisanal cheeses, prosciutto, focaccia, olives, and a chilled bottle of Frascati white wine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mirabelle Restaurant (Hotel Splendide Royal, Via Veneto) — a Michelin-recognized rooftop restaurant offering refined Italian haute cuisine with sweeping views over Rome's rooftops. An unmissable luxury dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery entry is strictly timed and limited to 360 visitors per 2-hour slot — advance booking is absolutely essential, often weeks ahead. Your hotel concierge should handle this immediately upon booking your trip. The gallery is approximately 25 minutes by taxi from the Borgo district.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Archaeological Walk — Embark on a private guided archaeological tour through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire. Begin at the Roman Forum, walking among the ruins of temples, the Via Sacra, and the Arch of Titus. Ascend to Palatine Hill — the legendary birthplace of Rome — for sweeping views and fascinating imperial palace ruins. A deeply immersive journey through 2,700 years of history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Colosseum VIP Experience — From Palatine Hill, walk directly to the Colosseum for an exclusive VIP access tour, including the arena floor and underground hypogeum (normally restricted). Stand where gladiators once fought and experience the scale and engineering genius of this ancient wonder up close with a private expert guide.
day_by_day.evening: Testaccio Neighborhood Food Exploration — Head to the authentic Testaccio district — Rome's traditional working-class culinary heart — for a curated evening of genuine Roman food culture, from the historic covered market to atmospheric local restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Caffè Sant'Eustachio (near the Pantheon, en route) — universally considered Rome's finest coffee. Their signature Gran Caffè is a transcendent experience. Pair with a warm cornetto alla crema.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Aroma Restaurant (Palazzo Manfredi, next to the Colosseum) — a Michelin-starred rooftop restaurant with arguably the most dramatic view of the Colosseum in all of Rome. An unforgettable premium lunch.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — a beloved Roman institution built into the ancient Monte Testaccio (a hill made entirely of ancient amphora shards). Exceptional traditional Roman cuisine including rigatoni con la pajata and coda alla vaccinara in a uniquely historic setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum VIP underground access well in advance through authorized operators — standard tickets do not include the hypogeum. The Forum/Palatine/Colosseum complex is approximately 30 minutes by taxi from Borgo. Wear comfortable walking shoes — this is a full day on ancient cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Pantheon, Piazza della Rotonda & Luxury Shopping — Begin with an unhurried morning visit to the Pantheon, one of the best-preserved ancient Roman buildings in the world. Admire the perfect geometry of its dome and the oculus that has let in rain and light for 2,000 years. Afterward, explore the luxury boutiques and artisan shops around Via Condotti, Piazza di Spagna (Spanish Steps), and Via Borgognona — Rome's premier high-fashion district.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trevi Fountain & Quirinal Hill — Visit the magnificent Trevi Fountain (most peaceful in the early afternoon) and toss your coin for good luck. Walk up to the Quirinal Hill for views over the city and a visit to the Palazzo del Quirinale gardens if open. Explore the elegant Via Veneto boulevard, Rome's legendary 1960s 'La Dolce Vita' street, lined with grand hotels and historic cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Gala Dinner — Reserve your most special dinner of the trip for this penultimate evening. Choose a rooftop or garden setting for a memorable final fine-dining experience under the Roman stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at La Caffetteria (Piazza di Pietra) — a refined café in a stunning ancient Roman temple setting. Exceptional pastries and coffee in an atmosphere that feels like a living museum.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Il Pagliaccio (near Piazza Navona) — Rome's most celebrated two-Michelin-starred restaurant, Chef Anthony Genovese's extraordinary fusion of Italian, Japanese, and French techniques. Book months in advance for this exceptional experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri Hotel, Monte Mario) — Rome's only three-Michelin-starred restaurant, Chef Heinz Beck's legendary establishment offering an unparalleled tasting menu with breathtaking panoramic views over the entire city. The pinnacle of luxury dining in Rome. Jacket required.

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola reservations are extremely competitive and should be booked as early as possible — ideally 2–3 months in advance. Your hotel concierge may have preferred access. Il Pagliaccio for lunch should also be booked well ahead. Via Condotti luxury shopping is approximately 20 minutes on foot or 10 minutes by taxi from the Borgo hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Slow Morning & Final Roman Rituals — Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at your boutique hotel. Take one last unhurried stroll through the Borgo Pio pedestrian lane, browse the charming antique and artisan shops near Castel Sant'Angelo, and perhaps revisit a favorite piazza or viewpoint. Pick up premium food souvenirs — aged cheeses, truffle products, artisanal pasta, and fine olive oil — from quality delis in the Prati neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Castel Sant'Angelo Final Visit & Departure Preparation — If time permits before checkout, visit the interior of Castel Sant'Angelo (steps from your hotel) — a fascinating fortress-museum with stunning rooftop views of St. Peter's and the Tiber. Return to hotel, complete checkout, and arrange private chauffeur transfer back to Fiumicino Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — Private chauffeur transfer to Leonardo da Vinci–Fiumicino Airport for your departing flight. Carry with you the flavors, artworks, and memories of seven extraordinary days in the Eternal City.

meals.breakfast: A long, indulgent final breakfast at your boutique hotel — savor every last espresso and cornetto. Alternatively, visit Pasticceria Borghese (Prati) for exceptional Roman pastries and a perfectly pulled cappuccino.
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Osteria dell'Ara Pacis (near the Ara Pacis museum, Prati area) — elegant modern Roman cuisine in a sophisticated setting overlooking the ancient Altar of Peace. A fitting, culturally rich final meal in Rome.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining — or if your flight departs late evening, enjoy a final casual dinner at a Prati enoteca such as Enoteca Ferrara, pairing a glass of Barolo with a Roman cheese and charcuterie board as your last taste of Italy.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with your boutique hotel and arrange luggage storage if needed for the morning's activities. Castel Sant'Angelo is literally steps from your hotel — a perfect, low-effort final experience. Rome traffic can be unpredictable; allow generous transfer time to the airport. Consider purchasing a curated Italian food and wine gift box from a Prati delicatessen as premium souvenirs.
